correction.text: Nabta Playa "approximately 800 kilometers south of modern-day Cairo", "about 100 kilometers west of Abu Simbel in southern Egypt"; coordinates 22 30 29 N 30 43 32 E; the "Nabta Playa-Bir Kiseiba area"; the part of the disc inside Egypt (the page places the site in Egypt; the part in Sudan is left to green-sahara-cultures), less the Nile-valley band (Upper Egypt, 40 km round the Nile) that naqada-culture draws, which the gazetteer's Nile line carries along the Lake Nasser arms

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. One 100 km disc cut at the Egyptian border and less the Naqada Nile band (75 land cells, about 18,975 km2) round the Nabta Playa coordinates in the Western Desert of Egypt, "about 100 kilometers west of Abu Simbel". The page gives the site and the "Nabta Playa-Bir Kiseiba area", not an area; the cattle there were "morphologically wild" or at most "semi-pastoralism", and the occupation was seasonal ("most likely only in the summer").

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the people of Nabta Playa already live round the playa lake in the Egyptian desert. "The Nabta Playa archaeological site, one of the earliest of the Nubian Neolithic Period, is dated to circa 7500 BC"; "Larger settlements began to appear at Nabta Playa by the 7th millennium BC, relying on deep wells". The culture begins before the floor.

5500 BCE: the Late Neolithic of Nabta Playa begins. "From 5500 BC the Late Neolithic period began"; the page lists "Late Neolithic (5400-4400 BC)" and says "Later pottery from c. 5500 BC (Al Jerar phase) has similarities with pottery from the Sudanese region."

4500 BCE: the megalith period begins at Nabta Playa. "More complex structures followed during a megalith period the researchers dated to between about 4500 BC to 3600 BC"; a stone circle was built "around 4800 BC".

ledger.note: 3600 BCE: the last dated megaliths of Nabta Playa. "a megalith period the researchers dated to between about 4500 BC to 3600 BC"; the page gives no end for the occupation ("page silent"), so the end is the last date it mentions and the land passes to nobody.

certainty.note: A seasonally occupied playa; no border is recorded.

notes: Nabta Playa Neolithic, Egyptian Western Desert. The page lists overlapping phase ranges ("Early Neolithic (8600-7050 BC)", "(7050-6100 BC)", "Middle Neolithic (6000-5500 BC)", "Late Neolithic (5400-4400 BC)") and does not name the Badari or Naqada; it gives no end of occupation, so -3600 (end of the megalith dates) is a floor, not a page date. The "Saharan cattle herders" are covered here for the Egyptian desert and by tenerian-culture for Niger. The gazetteer lacks the place name Nabta Playa (and Abu Simbel); a coordinate disc is used. The cattle of Nabta "have been shown to be morphologically wild in several studies" (Brass 2018: hunted aurochs), so the dossier is a desert-camp culture, not proven cattle herders. Second page (Prehistoric Egypt, opened 2026-10-18): "The Nabta Playa archaeological site, one of the earliest of the Egyptian Neolithic Period, is dated to circa 7500 BC"; cattle burials in subterranean chambers c. 5500 BC; and, in its timeline, "An aridification event in the Sahara leads to human migration to the Nile Valley" at c. 3900 BC, which is earlier than the 3600 BCE end used here (the last megalith date on the Nabta Playa page); a gap-filler may prefer 3900.
